notes: Verified against a throwaway postgres:16 container: both new integration tests pass on HEAD; TestMaintenanceRequeuesARebuildThatLostADeadlock fails on main's maintenance.go (`a lost deadlock is not a failure to report: ERROR: deadlock detected (SQLSTATE 40P01)`), so it genuinely exercises the fix.

internal/service/maintenance_test.go:167 TestMaintenanceFailsARebuildOutOfAttempts also passes on main's code — it is a guard for the retry bound, not a regression test; acceptable but it does not prove the new branch on its own.

internal/service/maintenance.go:104 a requeued job returns (false, nil), which ends the whole drain pass in Run(); other pending jobs wait up to one 15s tick. Documented in the RunPending comment; intentional, minor throughput cost.

internal/service/maintenance.go:98-99 if the requeue UPDATE itself fails the job stays 'running' with started_at set; it is only recovered by the 30-minute 'recovered after interrupted worker' sweep at startup, not by the running loop. Pre-existing shape of the failure path, not a regression.
internal/service/maintenance.go:118 semantics: Attempts < 10 → 9 requeues, 10 executions total; the comment's 'how many times ... put back' is off by one but harmless.

Test deadlock construction relies on Postgres choosing the longer-waiting transaction (the rebuild) as the victim; the test asserts this explicitly and it held in 3 runs, but could flake under heavy load. Skips without MOMENTO_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN like the other integration tests.
Scope is tight: only maintenance.go plus its new test; no migration needed (attempts column already exists in 001/009); fully revertable.
